newsitem.title: UK: British Steel active on steel shake-up hopes.
newsitem.headline: British Steel active on steel shake-up hopes.

text.p: British Steel Plc shares were busy on Tuesday as a bid by Germany's Krupp AG for Thyssen AG raised hopes of a shake-out in the European steel industry, analysts said.
British Steel gave a broadly positive reception to the bid, which would create Europe's third largest steelmaker, but said it had not seen much detail on the proposal.
"Anything that could lead to a reduction in capacity in Europe we would see as a potential positive," said a British Steel spokesman, but declined further comment.
By 1400 GMT British Steel shares were up 4p at 158 in volume of 9.2 million shares, making it the fourth most active stock in the FTSE 100 index.
Krupp confirmed earlier speculation of a bid, saying it was confident the bid would succeed.

"People are saying if the German bid happens it would be a good platform to take out some capacity," said one analyst. "It is a big problem in Europe that capacity exceeds demand. A rationalisation is overdue."
